Eisenhower Portfolio Manager — API Documentation

Overview

The Eisenhower Portfolio Manager is an enterprise-grade web application designed for defence programme management. It provides a complete backend API for managing portfolios, projects, tasks, resources, and locations through a unified hierarchical data model.

The system is built for use in classified operational environments (SCIFs — Sensitive Compartmented Information Facilities) where standard browser storage is prohibited and all user preferences must be persisted server-side.

Key Capabilities

  • Unified Tree Data Model — Portfolios, resources, and locations are stored in a single polymorphic hierarchy using PostgreSQL’s ltree extension, enabling efficient ancestor/descendant queries.

  • Critical Path Method (CPM) Scheduling — Automatic schedule calculation using forward and backward passes, with support for all four dependency types (FS, SS, FF, SF), lag/lead days, and a working calendar that skips weekends. Includes DCMA 14-Point integrity checks.

  • Attribute-Based Access Control (ABAC) — Fine-grained security that restricts data access based on user clearance levels and security caveats. When a user lacks clearance for an intermediate node but has clearance for its children, the parent is shown as a “ghost node” with redacted data, preserving the tree structure for the frontend.

  • Forensic Audit Logging — Every mutation to the data hierarchy is recorded in an immutable audit trail with SHA-256 chained hashing, making tampering detectable.

  • Server-Side Display Profiles — User display preferences (theme, density, color accessibility) are stored in PostgreSQL and hydrated on login, supporting hot-desking in terminal environments.

  • Daily Cockpit Dashboard — Personal landing page endpoints that provide each user with their active tasks, focus queue ordered by critical path priority, claimable placeholder tasks, and quick progress/blocker updates.

Security Architecture

The system implements multiple layers of security:

  1. Authentication — JWT-based authentication with bcrypt password hashing.

  2. Role-Based Access Control (RBAC) — Users have roles (Admin, Manager, Member, Viewer) that control administrative actions.

  3. Attribute-Based Access Control (ABAC) — Each data node carries a security classification (OFFICIAL through TOP_SECRET) and optional caveats (e.g., UK_EYES_ONLY). Users must have matching clearance to access data.

  4. Forensic Audit Trail — All data mutations are logged with chained SHA-256 hashes, creating a tamper-evident record.

Data Model

The core data model revolves around the Universal Breakdown Node (UBN), an abstract base that supports three specialised sub-types:

  • PortfolioNode (WBS) — Represents work packages, projects, and programmes with scheduling and Earned Value Management (EVM) fields.

  • ResourceNode (RBS) — Represents people, facilities, and assets with rate and availability information.

  • LocationNode (LBS) — Represents physical locations in a hierarchical structure, with SCIF/TEMPEST classification flags.

Secondary entities include:

  • DependencyLink — Precedence relationships between portfolio nodes.

  • ResourceAssignment — Links resources to portfolio nodes with allocation details.

  • NodeBlocker — Tracks impediments blocking progress on tasks.

  • ForensicAuditLog — Immutable audit trail with SHA-256 chained hashing.

API Endpoints

The API is organised into the following groups:

  • Authentication — User registration, login, and session management.

  • Users — User management and clearance administration.

  • Display Settings — Server-side display profile persistence.

  • WBS (Work Breakdown Structure) — Tree queries with ABAC filtering.

  • Schedule — CPM recalculation and schedule analysis.

  • Cockpit — Personal daily landing page endpoints.

System Requirements

  • Python 3.10+

  • PostgreSQL 12+ with the ltree extension enabled

  • FastAPI web framework with Uvicorn ASGI server

Getting Started

  1. Install dependencies:

    pip install -r requirements.txt

  2. Configure the database connection in .env:

    DATABASE_URL=postgresql+psycopg2://user:password@localhost:5432/eisenhower

  3. Initialise the database:

    python init_db.py --seed

  4. Start the server:

    uvicorn app.main:app --reload
